title: QBR Playbook + Renewal Tracker Templates (Standard & Enterprise)
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook + slide-outline collection for Customer Success Managers to run repeatable QBRs and manage renewals. Two deck flavors are included: a fast ‘Standard’ QBR for growth/SMB accounts and a deeper ‘Enterprise’ QBR for strategic, multi-stakeholder customers. Also included: a lightweight renewal tracker template and an action-oriented playbook for pre/during/post QBR activity and renewal negotiation signals.

Notes to reader (quick):
- This is a living doc — use as a starting point.
- Keep slides light: data + 1–2 callouts.
- For enterprise customers, include an appendix with technical details and SLOs.
- Use health-score buckets to prioritize outreach (Green/Yellow/Red).

1) Standard QBR (30–45 minutes) — slide outline + presenter notes
- Title / Executive Snapshot (1 slide)
  - One-liner outcome this quarter; renewal status (At-Risk / On-Track / Closed-Won); next milestone
  - Presenter note: Start with wins to reset framing.
- Agenda & Goals for Today (1 slide)
  - What we’ll cover: adoption highlights, usage trends, blockers, asks/next steps
- Account Health at a glance (1 slide)
  - Key KPIs: weekly active users, tokens/requests per week, error rate, latency P50/P95
  - Health score: 85 (Green) with short explanation
- Usage + Value Stories (2 slides)
  - Top 3 use cases delivering measurable value (revenue uplift, time saved)
  - Callout: customer quote or internal success snippet
- Risks & Blockers (1 slide)
  - Current incidents, technical debt, open tickets, org changes
  - Owner and ETA for resolution
- Roadmap alignment & upcoming features (1 slide)
  - Short list of Redwood roadmapped items relevant to them (e.g., lower-latency model variant, dedicated caching)
- Renewal & Commercial (1 slide)
  - Renewal date, ARR at stake, recommended renewal approach (auto-renew / negotiate / executive outreach)
  - Pricing levers we can offer (dedicated seat, burst capacity)
- Ask & Next Steps (1 slide)
  - Concrete next actions, owners, deadlines
- Appendix / Resources (1 slide)
  - Links to support tickets, docs, dataset example, playbook links

Presenter tips: keep data visual (trends, small tables). End with a single, prioritized ask. If renewal is within 90 days escalate to AE.

2) Enterprise QBR (60–75 minutes) — slide outline + presenter notes
- Title + Executive Summary (1 slide)\  - High-level outcome, renewal posture, key exec ask (e.g., expand to two more teams)
- Attendees & Decisions Needed (1 slide)
  - Who’s in the room, who is the economic decision-maker, technical decision-maker, procurement owner
- Business Impact Dashboard (2 slides)
  - Top-line metrics mapped to customer objectives (revenue saved, agent deflection, conversion uplift)\  - ROI projection for next 12 months using current adoption trajectory
- Deep Usage & Signals (3 slides)
  - Product paths: breakdown by integration points, API vs SDK usage, peak patterns\  - Performance matrix: latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, model variant distribution
- Reliability & Compliance Review (2 slides)
  - Incidents in last 6 months, mitigations, SLA attainment, audit items (if private deployment)\  - Security posture and upcoming compliance milestones (SOC2, GDPR notes)
- Technical Appendix Preview (1 slide)
  - Planned appendix topics: architecture diagram, integration checklist, scaling recommendations
- Renewal Strategy & Commercial Options (2 slides)
  - Contract timeline, recommended negotiation play (e.g., 12→24 month commit for 10% discount), cross-sell/upsell plays\  - Pricing sensitivity table: what we can trade (support hours, retention, price)
- Risk Matrix & Escalation Plan (1 slide)
  - Red flags: new procurement lead, budget reforecast, security audit flagged\  - Contingency: holdback terms, transition assistance, executive sponsor intro
- Customer Roadmap Collaboration (1 slide)
  - Co‑development opportunities, pilot proposals, PoC timelines
- Executive Ask & Signposts (1 slide)
  - Specific exec-level asks (intro to CTO, procurement timeline alignment)
- Action Plan & Owners (1 slide)
  - Clear RACI for next 90 days
- Appendix: Detailed metrics, logs, SRE runbook (separate doc)

Enterprise presenter tips: send pre-read 48 hours before meeting. Share a 1-page executive summary at the top of the deck as the first attachment. Bring an AE and a Solutions Engineer to handle commercial and technical questions.

3) Renewal Tracker (lightweight template — copy into sheet)
Columns described (use in a Google Sheet with one row per account):
- account_name
- cs_owner
- ae_owner
- renewal_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- renewal_value (ARR / contract value)
- current_term_months
- renewal_status (prospecting / working / sent-proposal / signed / lost)
- health_score (Green/Yellow/Red)
- last_qbr_date
- next_qbr_date
- top_risks (short bullets separated by | )
- decision_contacts (role:name pairs separated by | )
- commercial_notes (what discount / concession discussed)
- next_action (owner:action:due_date)
- escalation_required (yes/no)
- notes_link (link to QBR deck or incident ticket)

Sample row (as text example)
- acme-inc | Priya Nayar | Evan Martinez | 2026-04-15 | $120k | 12 | working | Yellow | 2025-11-20 | 2026-02-10 | latency spike during demo | CTO:Mary Chen| proposed 10% discount for 24 mo commit | Priya:send-proposal:2026-02-18 | yes | https://drive.redwood/qbr/acme-2025-q4

Operational rules for tracker
- Sort by renewal_date asc and flag anything within 90 days as high priority.
- Health_score must be updated after every major incident or significant usage change.
- AE must be tagged in tracker row if renewal_value > $50k.
- Weekly CS ops sync to review top 10 at-risk accounts.

4) Playbook: pre / during / post QBR and renewal negotiation steps
Pre-QBR (2–4 weeks out)
- Run data pack: usage trends (90/30/7 day), error logs, support tickets, feature adoption heatmap
- Send pre-read: 1-page exec summary + 10-slide deck draft 48 hours before meeting
- Confirm attendees and decisions needed; escalate invite to exec sponsor if not confirmed 1 week out
- Health calibration call with SRE/SE if any open incidents or performance risk
- Prep commercial scenarios: baseline renewal, expansion scenario, defensive scenario (price concessions + value add)

During QBR
- Start with exec summary and 1 ask only
- Use data to validate outcomes (metrics -> business impact)
- Timebox the technical deep dive; capture follow-up items in tracker
- If renewal discussion begins, move commercial negotiation to separate follow-up session with AE (don’t negotiate pricing in same slot unless pre-agreed)

Post-QBR (24–72 hours)
- Email recap with decisions, owners, and deadlines within 24 hours (template below)
- Update renewal tracker row and set cadence for weekly touchpoints if renewal in next 90 days
- Create PO/contract checklist for AE + legal if commitment requested
- For at-risk customers: schedule 1:1 with executive sponsor and document remediation plan

Renewal negotiation play (skeleton)
1. Qualification: confirm budget window and procurement timeline.
2. Optioning: present 2 commercial options (conservative & growth) with quantified ROI for each.
3. Trade-space: identify non-price concessions we can offer (additional support hours, extended onboarding, feature sandbox access).
4. Formal proposal: AE sends terms, CS ensures tech appendix is attached, 48–72 hour expected review window.
5. Close & kickoff: once signed route to onboarding/solutions team for expansion or renew-only path.

Risk signals (automated + manual)
- Sudden drop in weekly active requests >30%
- Increase in error rate >2x baseline or P95 latency > 2x SLA
- New procurement lead / budget reforecast noted in customer emails
- Multiple high-severity incidents in last 60 days without remediation

Communication templates (short)
- Invite (48h pre-read request)
  Subject: QBR + renewal pulse — [Account] — Proposal to meet [date]
  Body: Hi [Name], would like to share a short exec summary and roadmap aligned to your goals. Pre-read attached, 45 minutes. Key decision: confirm renewal posture and next steps for expansion.

- 24h follow-up recap
  Subject: QBR recap — actions and owners — [Account] — [Date]
  Body: Thanks for your time today. Highlights: win 1; health: Yellow (latency). Decisions: AE to send proposal by [date]. Owners: Priya (tech follow-up), Evan (commercial). Next meeting: [date]. Doc: [link]

- Executive escalation (example)
  Subject: Request: Exec intro to accelerate renewal — [Account]
  Body: Quick ask — customer is evaluating options and requests exec-level confirmation on roadmap/timeline. Recommended intro: [name], reason: procurement timeline 4 weeks.

5) Quick appendix: health-score rubric (suggested)
- Green: usage growth >10% q/q, SLOs met, 0 high sev incidents last 90 days
- Yellow: flat or down usage, 1-2 medium incidents, minor SLA misses
- Red: sustained drop (>20%), repeated high-sev incidents, procurement changes

6) TODOs / open questions (notes to self)
- Need canonical slide deck template in the docs repo (Priya -> DOCS-88)
- Add a column for trial vs production usage in tracker (Evan)
- Decide whether we allow pricing negotiations inside QBR or require separate call (stakeholder: AE lead)
- Build automation: health_score calculation from telemetry (SRE + CS ops)

End of doc.

Version history (short)
- 2025-11-15 initial draft by Priya
- 2025-12-02 added renewal tracker columns and sample row (Evan)
- 2026-01-20 appended enterprise escalation matrix and templates (Leah)
